summary: Imidapril is an oral angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor prodrug used for the treatment of essential hypertension (and, in some regions, diabetic nephropathy and chronic heart failure). After absorption it is converted to its active metabolite imidaprilat, which inhibits ACE, reducing formation of the vasoconstrictor angiotensin II and decreasing aldosterone secretion, thereby lowering peripheral vascular resistance and blood pressure. The usual starting dose for hypertension is 5 mg once daily, with a usual maintenance dose of 10 mg once daily and a maximum of 20 mg daily. Like other ACE inhibitors, it can cause a dry cough, hyperkalemia, renal impairment, first-dose hypotension, and rare but serious angioedema, and it is contraindicated in pregnancy. NOTE: imidapril is not approved by the US FDA; this record is based on European SmPC/BNF-type sources.
indications: Chronic heart failure as adjunctive therapy (in some regional approvals)

moa: Imidapril is an orally administered prodrug that is hydrolyzed (mainly in the liver) to its active diacid metabolite, imidaprilat. Imidaprilat is a potent inhibitor of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE, kininase II). By inhibiting ACE, it blocks the conversion of angiotensin I to the potent vasoconstrictor angiotensin II, reduces aldosterone secretion (promoting sodium/water excretion and potassium retention), and decreases the breakdown of bradykinin. The net effect is vasodilation, reduced peripheral vascular resistance, and lowering of blood pressure, with reduced cardiac afterload.

absolute: Pregnancy (second and third trimesters; not recommended in first trimester)
History of angioedema (hereditary, idiopathic, or related to previous ACE inhibitor therapy)
Hypersensitivity to imidapril or other ACE inhibitors
Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with diabetes mellitus or moderate-to-severe renal impairment
Concomitant use with sacubitril/valsartan (or within 36 hours)
relative: Bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis to a single functioning kidney
Significant renal impairment, hyperkalemia, or hypovolemia
Aortic/mitral valve stenosis or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (outflow obstruction)
Severe hepatic impairment; collagen vascular disease (neutropenia risk)
monitor: Signs of angioedema (facial, lip, tongue, laryngeal swelling)

preg: Imidapril is contraindicated in pregnancy. ACE inhibitors used in the second and third trimesters can cause fetal renal failure, oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia, hypotension, and death. Even first-trimester exposure may carry risk. Women planning pregnancy should be switched to an alternative antihypertensive, and the drug should be stopped immediately if pregnancy is confirmed.
lact: Use during breastfeeding is not recommended, particularly when nursing a newborn or preterm infant, because of limited data and the potential for neonatal hypotension and renal effects. If used, choose an alternative with better-established safety, or avoid breastfeeding.
renal: In renal impairment, reduce the dose (start around 2.5 mg once daily) and titrate carefully with monitoring of renal function and potassium. ACE inhibitors can acutely worsen renal function, especially in renal artery stenosis, hypovolemia, or with NSAIDs; avoid in severe or bilateral renal artery stenosis.
hepatic: Because imidapril is a prodrug requiring hepatic activation to imidaprilat, hepatic impairment may alter both activation and clearance. Use with caution, start at a low dose, and monitor blood pressure response and tolerability.

major: Aliskiren in diabetes or moderate-severe renal impairment - contraindicated (dual RAAS blockade)
Sacubitril/valsartan - contraindicated (angioedema risk); separate by at least 36 hours
Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes - severe hyperkalemia
moderate: Other diuretics/antihypertensives - additive hypotension (especially first dose)
NSAIDs - reduced antihypertensive effect and increased risk of renal impairment and hyperkalemia
Lithium - reduced lithium clearance and lithium toxicity
Other RAAS-acting agents (ARBs) - increased hyperkalemia and renal risk
minor: Antidiabetic agents (insulin, sulfonylureas) - possible enhanced hypoglycemic effect
interactions.food: Food may reduce absorption; take before a meal. Avoid high-potassium salt substitutes.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may enhance the blood-pressure-lowering effect; advise moderation.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum potassium and creatinine; ACE inhibitors may affect these. Rarely cause neutropenia (monitor in at-risk patients).

serious: Angioedema (face, lips, tongue, larynx) - potentially life-threatening
Symptomatic hypotension, especially in volume-depleted patients

monitoring: Blood pressure at initiation and during titration (first-dose hypotension)
Renal function (creatinine, eGFR) before and after starting and with dose changes
Serum potassium, especially with renal impairment or potassium-affecting drugs
Signs of angioedema and persistent cough
White cell count in patients with collagen vascular disease or renal impairment
counsel: Take this medicine before food at the same time each day, even if you feel well
A dry, tickly cough can occur - tell your doctor if it is bothersome, as a different medicine may be needed
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down, especially after your first doses, to avoid dizziness
Seek emergency care immediately if you notice swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing
Do not use this medicine if you are or may become pregnant; avoid potassium-based salt substitutes and tell your doctor about any other medicines, especially painkillers (NSAIDs)
pk: Antihypertensive effect within hours; full effect over weeks of regular dosing
Active metabolite imidaprilat peaks several hours after dosing
Imidaprilat has a long effective half-life supporting once-daily dosing
Blood-pressure lowering maintained over 24 hours with once-daily dosing
Store below 25-30 C in original packaging; protect from moisture (per SmPC)
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - this record is based on European SmPC/BNF-type sources; imidapril is marketed in Europe and Asia, not the United States
Prodrug activated to imidaprilat - hepatic impairment can affect activation; start low
Class effects apply: dry cough, hyperkalemia, renal impairment, first-dose hypotension, and rare angioedema
Contraindicated in pregnancy and with aliskiren (in diabetes/renal impairment) or sacubitril/valsartan
Food reduces absorption - dose before meals; avoid NSAIDs and potassium salt substitutes
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual once-daily schedule - do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Overdose may cause marked hypotension, shock, electrolyte disturbances (hyperkalemia), and renal failure. Management is supportive: place the patient supine, restore intravascular volume with intravenous saline, and treat persistent hypotension with appropriate measures. Imidaprilat may be removed to some extent by hemodialysis. Monitor blood pressure, potassium, and renal function closely.
